thread:
Priya: Quick follow-up on the svc auth RFC — we need to pick a canonical pattern for service-to-service auth (project-scoped API keys vs short-lived JWTs issued by the control plane). Goal: minimize blast radius for Dedicated/Private customers and make rotation/impersonation simple.
Marco: +1 we should also factor in offline/air-gapped deploys. Keys might be the only option there.
Ava: Proposal idea: long-lived "proj_api_key" (scoped to project/org) used only to mint short-lived service tokens (svc_jwt) via local CA, with minting restricted by role. Long-lived keys are stored in KMS/HSM.
Sam: Sounds reasonable. A few questions: 1) who can mint? 2) how do we handle cross-project calls? 3) audit/logging?
Priya: 1) mint role = service principal + explicit project allow list. 2) cross-project = scoped delegation tokens with explicit "aud" and limited ops. 3) audit = emit mint events to customer audit log + control plane, tie to key id and issuer.
Jules: For private/on-prem we can't assume control-plane connectivity. Suggest a local CA mode where a signed CA cert is stored in a secure enclave, and the long-lived key mints tokens locally. Ops still writes mint events to local audit store; Control plane gets synced when network available.
Marco: Edge case: what if a compromised container has the proj_api_key? Even with local minting, attacker can mint tokens. We should make proj_api_key usage observable and rate-limited + optional IP constraints.
Ava: Agree. Add requirements: - Default proj_api_keys are disabled for direct use by services (must call mint endpoint). - Mint endpoint enforces MFA for humans and RBAC for services. - Rate limit by key_id and by project.
Sam: Is there a clear schema for the tokens? I propose JWT with header {"alg":"HS256"|"RS256","kid":"<key-id>"}, claims: iss, sub, aud (target project), scope (comma list), exp, nbf, x-origin-key (proj key id). Example:
```
Authorization: Bearer svc_eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6InByb2pfMTIzIn0.eyJpc3MiOiJyZWR3b29k-control","sub":"svc:billing/ingest","aud":"project:acme-prod","scope":"ingest.write,kv.read","exp":1690000000,"xok":"proj_abc123"
```
Priya: +1 to including x-origin-key. That makes rotation easier (revoke by proj key id). Also recommend short lifetimes (1-15m) for svc_jwt, configurable by policy.
Jules: Rotation: we should support key versioning: proj_abc123.v1, .v2. Minted tokens carry the vX so control plane can reject tokens signed by revoked key versions.
Marco: What about RBAC model vs capability scopes? If we keep coarse roles (admin, writer, reader) we lose principle of least privilege. Capabilities (ingest.write) are better but explode permission graph. Tradeoff?
Ava: Hybrid: role == collection of capability scopes. Keep capability-based checks at the service layer, but expose role templates for common bundles. This helps UI and policy mgmt.
Sam: Implementation note: runtime checks should prefer capability checks, but we keep role checks for high-level gate (e.g., can this principal mint any token at all).
Priya: One more: impersonation. We want a way for services to act on behalf of a user with explicit consent. Suggest minting a user-scoped token where issuer is control-plane and x-origin-key references user consent record id. Short TTL and must include original user id.
Marco: Logging: every mint should emit: key_id, requester_principal, target_aud, scopes, ttl, result (success/fail), and IP. Store in immutable log with retention policy per customer.
Ava: Security controls checklist: KMS-backed storage; HSM for private keys in private deployments; rotation tooling; revocation endpoint that marks key versions revoked; mint endpoint RBAC and rate-limit; audit export hooks.
Sam: UX: CLI helpers to create proj_api_key with --scopes, --ip-allowlist, --ttl, and a rotate command. Docs and console flows needed.
Jules: Ops-bot: deploy job for CA rotation needs coordination window. bots: please add runbook.
ops-bot: @channel runbook created: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/ca-rotation — includes preflight checks, rollout steps, and rollback.
Priya: Next steps: write short RFC appendix covering token format, mint flow diagram, edge cases (air-gapped, revoked+race conditions), and a backwards-compatible rollout plan. I'll draft and share by EOD tomorrow. Please comment on the draft when I post it. :thumbsup:
Marco: Thanks — will review.
Ava: I'll add the HSM integration section.
Sam: I'll prototype the mint endpoint and a sample CLI.
Jules: I'll draft the audit schema and retention options.
Priya: Awesome — closing the loop here. If anyone thinks we've missed an obvious attack vector speak up now.
Marco: minor: consider key leakage detection via anomaly scoring of mint patterns (spike detection).
Ava: noted.
Sam: Also add header-based mutual TLS verification for cross-project calls when possible.
Priya: Great, thanks everyone.
